name: Karres
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny highland village above the Imst Gorge featuring historic mining roots, Mount Tschirgant vistas, and easy river rafting access.
beschreibung:
Overview

Karres sits at an altitude of 830 metres on a sun-drenched terrace in the Tyrolean Oberinntal within the district of Imst. Home to approximately 640 residents, this peaceful village clings to the south-eastern foothills of Mount Tschirgant and overlooks the entrance to the world-renowned Imst Gorge. Directly opposite, the Pitze River joins the mighty Inn, affording sweeping panoramic views across the Inn Valley, the entrance to the Pitztal, and the rugged peaks flanking the Ötztal. Karres captivates visitors with its quiet seclusion away from heavy transit, preserving authentic rural customs alongside immediate access to celebrated outdoor adventures throughout western Tyrol.

History

The settlement was first mentioned in historical records in 1288 in the land registry of Count Meinhard II of Tyrol under the name 'Cherres'. The toponym has pre-Roman origins, indicating ancient human presence on this sheltered mountain shelf. Between the late fifteenth and nineteenth centuries, Karres played an important role in regional mining operations along the slopes of the Tschirgant. Miners extracted galena for Tyrolean silver smelting as well as zinc ores. In the village centre, several heritage-protected miners' houses with stout stone walls recall this prosperous era under Emperor Maximilian I. The late-Gothic Parish Church of Saint Stephen, recorded as early as 1447, features a striking church tower dating to 1583 and fine Baroque altars. Nearby, a preserved paved section of the eighteenth-century imperial postal highway remains a protected monument.

Getting There

Motorists can reach Karres via the Inntal Autobahn A12, exiting at either Haiming/Ötztal or Imst-Ost/Roppen. From there, the B171 Federal Highway and the L243 Karrer Landesstraße ascend gently in just a few minutes onto the plateau. Rail travellers arrive via the Imst-Pitztal railway station, located only 3.5 kilometres away along the Arlberg rail line, or Roppen station. Regional bus route 320 operated by the VVT links Karres with Imst bus terminal and local rail stations on a regular schedule. Cyclists can also reach the village via hillside connector routes leading up from the scenic Inn Cycle Path R1.

Tips

Directly beneath Karres lies the Imst Gorge, recognized as one of the premier whitewater rafting stretches in Europe. Exhilarating commercial raft and kayak tours navigate the turbulent currents and towering rock faces of the Inn River. For hikers, the towering summit of Mount Tschirgant at 2,370 metres provides an irresistible challenge. The main trail ascends through alpine meadows to the welcoming Karrer Alm at 1,648 metres, where hikers enjoy hearty Tyrolean platters on the panoramic terrace. From the summit ridge, walkers are rewarded with an extraordinary 360-degree vista spanning the Inn Valley, the Mieming plateau, and the Lechtal Alps. For a leisurely outing, explore the historic paved imperial road toward Roppen or stroll among the centuries-old miners' dwellings.
